hero.title: Flipping is Hard
hero.description: Flipping is Hard is the Foddian-style rage platformer from Elegant Horse Studios: you are Flippy, a '90s flip phone lost in the land of lost things, climbing back toward your owner Jeff — and rotation is your only movement. No legs, no walking, no jumping; just flips, falls and the climb, through ten surreal areas, solo or with up to 32 players in online co-op. Released in October 2026 on Steam, this wiki covers it from day one: how the flipping actually works, the areas and their tricks, the co-op chaos, and how it stands in the Getting Over It lineage.

aboutGame.title: What Is Flipping is Hard?
paragraphs: Flipping is Hard is a precision platformer — a rage game, in the community's honest vocabulary — from Elegant Horse Studios, a studio out of Vilnius, Lithuania. You play Flippy, a '90s flip phone, lost in the land of lost things and climbing to return to his owner, Jeff. The hook is the control scheme: rotation is your only movement. Flippy has no legs and no jump button; every meter of the climb is earned by flipping, building momentum, landing at angles that stick, and eating the falls that come when they don't.

The game released in October 2026 on Steam, climbing through ten surreal areas either solo or with up to 32 players in online co-op. It belongs to the Foddian lineage — Getting Over It's school of one-mistake-falls and earned mastery — and it wears the genre's cruelty with a '90s-object warmth that keeps the rage funny. This wiki covers it from launch: the flipping mechanics, the areas, the co-op, and the culture around the climb.

items.question: What is Flipping is Hard?
items.answer: A Foddian-style rage platformer by Elegant Horse Studios. You play Flippy, a '90s flip phone climbing through the land of lost things to return to his owner Jeff — using rotation as your only movement, through 10 surreal areas, solo or with up to 32 players in online co-op.

items.question: Is Flipping is Hard out?
items.answer: Yes — it fully released in October 2026 on Steam, with a launch discount running at release. This wiki has covered it since launch day, and its pages update as the community maps the climb.

items.question: Is it too hard for me?
items.answer: It is hard — that is the game's name and its honest warning. But the difficulty is mastery-based rather than gated: every fall teaches, every meter is earned, and the players who finish are the ones who kept flipping, not the ones with special reflexes. The tips and mindset page exists precisely for this question.

items.question: Does co-op make it easier?
items.answer: It makes it different. Up to 32 players share the climb — company for the falls, witnesses for the wins, and a comedy that solo cannot match — but each player's flips remain their own. The co-op guide covers what changes and what doesn't.
